title: 2019 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: Right triangle \(ACD\) with right angle at \(C\) is constructed outwards on the hypotenuse \(\overline{AC}\) of isosceles right triangle \(ABC\) with leg length \(1,\) as shown, so that the two triangles have equal perimeters. What is \(\sin(2\angle BAD)?\)

solutions.text:
Triangle \(ABC\) has perimeter \(1+1+\sqrt2=2+\sqrt2\) and \(AC=\sqrt2.\) In \(\triangle ACD\) let \(CD=d,\) so \(AD=\sqrt{2+d^2}\) and equal perimeters give \[ \sqrt2+d+\sqrt{2+d^2}=2+\sqrt2. \]

Then \(\sqrt{2+d^2}=2-d,\) so \(2+d^2=4-4d+d^2,\) giving \(d=\dfrac12\) and \(AD=\dfrac32.\)

Since \(\angle BAC=45^\circ,\) writing \(\theta=\angle CAD\) gives \(2\angle BAD=90^\circ+2\theta,\) so \(\sin(2\angle BAD)=\cos 2\theta.\) With \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{CD}{AC}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt2},\) we get \[ \begin{gathered} \cos2\theta=\dfrac{1-\tan^2\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta} \\ =\dfrac{1-\tfrac18}{1+\tfrac18}=\dfrac{7}{9}. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: \(\triangle ABC\) has legs \(1\) and hypotenuse \(AC=\sqrt2;\) set \(CD=d\) and use equal perimeters
